title: Kid Lips Hackett, showman drummer and prizefighter
summary: Jones describes Kid Lips Hackett as a flipping, juggling showman who could also play symphony, and the act he planned with Sid Catlett.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: That's very interesting. We've really covered a great deal of drummers here, haven't we? Can you think of anybody in the line of drums whom we've omitted? Do you want me to call off some names for you?

He played with everything. In the days in show business annals and TOBA and all that, all they wanted to know, did you have a sensational drummer. This is a drummer that could flip the sticks, run around the room, juggle the sticks and do all that business, but at the same time you must be able to play "Poet and Peasant" too. You must be able to play a symphony. You must remember, like in the early days of semipro baseball, in order for a baseball player - black - to do anything he had to clown, as they call it. It wasn't a clown. He had to do a little simple thing called showmanship. He had to have a certain flair, the way he slid into the bases, the way he caught a ball, or the way he wore his cap. You see what I mean? It's no different than the kids today to try to get an identity, to put on the cowboy suits or what have you... But I didn't know that this man, till later, he not only could write music and write drum parts, but he could play the whole bit. He could sit in and play with a straight orchestra and still do his act. You see, he had an act.

He was a terrific prizefighter. When the people on the show would be stranded and nothing happen, he'd book himself down at the YMCA or some club somewhere and go and pick up $20 or $25 and come back and feed somebody, and come back and still do the show. Ironically, a little girl with a penknife, in Cincinnati - he said, "Come on, you girls, and do the show," and she had a little penknife and she stuck it in his side. He bled internally. He was like the fighter they used to call the Angel, that could wind up speak 7 languages and with the most beautiful girl? Like Bull Moose Jackson, "you're so ugly you're beautiful." He was a beautiful man. At one time Sid Catlett, Kid Lips Hackett and myself were going to make an act and we were going to quit the band, any band, any show that we was with. We were going to go out and have a triangle and we were going to go out and book ourselves on the circuit, at one time. Sid could play a little piano, we'd play anything, "Liza" or anything on there, just play some stop time and we'd be jumping around. The lights would be on us. We had 15 minutes that we could do and we figured out that we didn't have to play with no band. We could go out and make ourselves the unheard salary of $200 a week. We could book that act for $650, man, we had a whole lot of money.
